Examples described in the TR include DGIWG Metadata Foundation, Defence Orthoimagery Product, Defence Gridded Elevation Data, service profiles and encoding profiles. These remain informative profile examples and are not represented as ISO 19121 domain classes.
The figure intentionally shows a selected set of ISO 19115-2 relationships for readability. The authoritative ISO 19115-2 package retains the complete metadata model.

External implementation standards referenced by the TR, including GeoTIFF/COG, OGC SensorThings/coverage APIs and model-portability standards such as ONNX/PMML, are shown here as informative textual references rather than fabricated ISO 19121 classes.
CNN, RNN and Transformer architectures are implementation techniques. They are not introduced as ISO 19121 application-schema classes.
This organizational collaboration figure is informative and does not introduce domain classes into the ISO 19121 application schema.

GeoTIFF, NetCDF, HDF, JPEG 2000, COG and other external encodings/formats remain informative references unless represented by an authoritative Harmonized Model element. They are not modelled here as ISO 19121 classes.

SE_SensorModel in ISO/DTS 19130-2 uses sensorDataModeling : SE_DataModelingMethod [0..1], sensorManufacturer : CharacterString [0..1], and version : CharacterString [1]. Multiplicity is stored on the UML property, not inside the datatype name.
This activity diagram replaces a class-based representation of processing tasks. It represents behaviour and workflow, not a domain inheritance hierarchy.

MODEL ARCHITECTURE
ISO 19121 reuses existing ISO/TC 211 Harmonized Model components wherever appropriate. Dependencies represent reuse or application-schema reliance and do not denote inheritance. ISO 19121-specific classifiers should be introduced only where an identified requirement cannot be satisfied by an existing Harmonized Model element.

High-level ISO 19121 package architecture. The central application schema depends on existing ISO/TC 211 Harmonized Model packages. Dependencies indicate reuse or application-schema reliance and do not denote inheritance.
Re-engineered core coverage model. All classifiers and relationships shown are linked directly from ISO 19123-1; no ISO 19121 copies are created.
Reuse view of ISO 19115-2 metadata, acquisition, platform, instrument, sensor, content and geolocation concepts relevant to imagery and gridded data.
Sensor-model reuse view resolving the HMMG concern about duplicated ISO 19130 classes and incorrect multiplicities. Canonical ISO 19130-1/2 classifiers are linked directly.
